katarina.h1: How to Play Katarina in League of Legends
heroIntro: Katarina is a high-mobility mid-lane assassin whose damage comes from daggers, resets and clean execution. She has no mana, so her limits are cooldowns, positioning and crowd control.

This guide covers her patch 26.21 builds, the level-by-level skill order, practical dagger combos, lane and teamfight decisions, and the matchups that punish careless entries. It is written for ranked Summoner's Rift and is based on Data Dragon 16.21.1 plus current U.GG and Lolalytics samples.
katarina.quickAnswer: Max Q first, then E, then W. Take Electrocute with Sudden Impact and Precision secondaries, start Dark Seal or Doran's Ring, and build Lich Bane into Shadowflame for burst. Play around dagger pickups and wait for enemy crowd control before committing. Katarina is strong on patch 26.21, but her win rate comes from patience and target selection, not from forcing every fight.

quickStart.keyMechanic: Dagger pickups reset Shunpo and trigger area damage
quickStart.beginnerMistake: Using E to engage with no exit route or without tracking enemy crowd control
quickStart.winCondition: Force a side-lane pick or a chaotic fight, then chain resets onto isolated carries

abilities.name: Voracity
abilities.description: Katarina's takedowns dramatically reduce her remaining cooldowns. Picking up a dagger slashes nearby enemies for magic damage.
tips: Track the landing spot before you commit.
Pick up daggers that also hit a champion.
A reset is not a safety guarantee.
abilities.mistake: Chasing a kill without checking where the dagger lands or who can punish the approach.

abilities.name: Bouncing Blade
abilities.description: Katarina throws a dagger that bounces to nearby enemies and lands on the ground.
tips: Use Q to farm and create a future dagger.
Watch the final landing position, not just the first hit.
Bouncing through a wave can push the dagger closer to your target.
abilities.mistake: Treating Q as pure poke and ignoring the dagger it leaves behind.

abilities.name: Preparation
abilities.description: Katarina gains movement speed and leaves a dagger above herself that falls after a short delay.
tips: Use the speed to dodge or reach a dagger.
Place W before you go in so the dagger covers your exit.
The dagger is a reset tool, not just a speed button.
abilities.mistake: Using W only for movement speed and never collecting the dagger.

abilities.name: Shunpo
abilities.description: Katarina blinks to a target, damaging it if it is an enemy, or the nearest enemy otherwise. Dagger pickups reduce its cooldown.
tips: Keep one jump available for escape.
Use enemy minions, allies and daggers as repositioning tools.
E to a dagger when the slash improves the trade.
abilities.mistake: Spending E as the first and only mobility option into a fight.

abilities.name: Death Lotus
abilities.description: Katarina channels a storm of blades, damaging the three nearest enemy champions.
tips: Wait for interrupts to be used.
Position so the blades hit valuable targets.
Cancel early if the channel is about to be punished.
abilities.mistake: Channeling into a team that still has reliable stuns or knockups.

explanation: Q is the safest way to farm, poke and set up daggers, so it is maxed first.
E ranks lower its cooldown and improve how often you can reposition around daggers.
W is maxed last because the movement-speed duration and cooldown matter less than the Q and E breakpoints.
skillOrder.note: This is the most common path on patch 26.21 in the U.GG and Lolalytics samples. In hard lanes, some players delay E for extra W safety; that is a matchup adjustment, not the default.

runes.title: Electrocute burst
runes.summary: Electrocute is the default keystone on patch 26.21. It gives Katarina a reliable burst window on short trades and helps her finish targets before they can answer. Precision secondary adds sustained damage and takedown value.

keystone.name: Electrocute
keystone.why: Best default for Q-E trades and assassination patterns.

primaryRunes.name: Sudden Impact
primaryRunes.why: Bonus penetration after Shunpo makes every short trade hit harder.

primaryRunes.name: Sixth Sense
primaryRunes.why: Free ward detection that helps you control river vision.

primaryRunes.name: Ultimate Hunter
primaryRunes.why: More Death Lotus casts in a snowballing game.

secondaryRunes.name: Triumph
secondaryRunes.why: Takedown healing and gold help Katarina keep chaining fights.

secondaryRunes.name: Coup de Grace
secondaryRunes.why: Extra damage to low-health targets improves reset chains.

alternatives: Hail of Blades for early auto trades and on-hit builds
Last Stand or Cut Down instead of Coup de Grace
Taste of Blood or Cheap Shot instead of Sudden Impact
notes: Rune choices vary by lobby. The page above is a common patch 26.21 setup, not the only correct page.
If you are learning Katarina, Electrocute is more forgiving than Dark Harvest because it does not require stacks.
Into heavy poke, Taste of Blood can replace Sudden Impact for lane sustain.

summonerSpells.name: Flash
summonerSpells.why: The default escape and engage tool. E alone is not enough to enter and leave safely.

summonerSpells.name: Ignite
summonerSpells.why: Adds kill pressure in lane and helps finish low-health targets before they heal or escape.
summonerSpells.alternative: Teleport is a safer option in lanes where you cannot trade early.

builds.label: AP burst

items.name: Health Potion

builds.label: AD and on-hit

Do not mix AP and on-hit items without a clear reason.

combos.name: Safe lane trade
combos.situation: A short lane trade or a safe poke window.
combos.execution: Throw Q so the dagger lands behind the target, E to the dagger or the champion, W for speed and a second dagger, auto once, then E to the W dagger or an ally minion to leave.
combos.mistake: Holding E until after you are already stunned.
combos.warning: Do not use this into a mage with a ready point-and-click stun.

combos.name: Two-dagger all-in
combos.situation: An all-in after the enemy has spent their main crowd control.
combos.execution: Place Q and W daggers, E onto the target, start R immediately, then collect daggers after the channel if the fight continues.
combos.mistake: Channeling R before the enemy's stun or knockup is used.
combos.warning: If the enemy can interrupt you, skip R and keep the daggers for a reset.

combos.name: Cleanup entry
combos.situation: Cleaning up a fight when a low-health target is isolated.
combos.execution: E to the target, Q immediately, W for speed and a dagger, then R. Use dagger pickups to reset E for the next target.
combos.mistake: Tunnel-visioning on the first kill and forgetting the next exit.

combos.name: Teamfight reset chain
combos.situation: Mid-game teamfights after the first crowd-control spells are used.
combos.execution: Enter from a flank, damage the closest priority target, pick up a dagger, then decide whether to continue or leave. Reset chains are a decision loop, not a fixed sequence.
combos.mistake: Jumping in just because a takedown happened.
combos.warning: A reset does not cleanse crowd control or make you invulnerable.

sections.heading: Laning phase: survive, farm, then move
paragraphs: Katarina's first three levels are about preserving health and setting up daggers, not forcing trades. Use Q to last-hit and bounce damage through the wave, and keep E for dodging or escaping. If the enemy walks past their minions, a Q-E-W trade can be worth it, but only when their key cooldown is down.

Against ranged mages, let the wave push toward you and farm with Q. Do not stand on top of your own dagger if the enemy can punish the pickup. When you have level 6 and Ignite, look for a kill window after the enemy uses their defensive spell or misses a key skillshot.

Roam when the wave is pushed and your lane opponent cannot follow quickly. Katarina's W movement speed and E make river fights dangerous for the enemy, but a failed roam costs you a full wave and tempo.
bullets: Keep the river brush warded before you push.
Do not E to a dagger if it puts you under the enemy tower.
Respect level 2 jungle ganks; Katarina has no natural escape without E.

sections.heading: Mid game: create the first pick
paragraphs: Katarina does not need to start fights. She wants the enemy to start one, or she wants to catch a carry rotating alone. Push a side wave, disappear from vision and hover near the river. The threat of your absence is often more valuable than a low-percentage dive.

When a fight starts, wait for the first wave of crowd control. Then enter from the side, target the lowest-risk high-value champion and keep track of your E cooldown. If no reset is available, leave before the enemy collapses.
bullets: Play around vision, not just damage.
Take one kill and reassess before chasing the second.
Buy control wards when you are ahead; Katarina's flanks need vision.

sections.heading: Teamfights: patience beats speed
paragraphs: The most common Katarina mistake is entering first. Her damage is high, but she is still a melee champion with no built-in crowd-control immunity. Let the enemy use their stuns, knockups and exhausts on your frontline or on the first engage.

Look for a flank angle that lets you reach the backline without walking through the enemy tank. Use Q and W to create daggers before you commit, and hold R until the enemy's interrupts are gone. If the fight is lost, use E to leave rather than chasing a highlight.
bullets: Track the enemy support's crowd control and the mid laner's stun.
Do not R into a target that can walk behind their frontline.
A dagger pickup that saves your life is worth more than one that deals extra damage.

matchups.note: Win rates below are from the U.GG and Lolalytics patch 26.21 Emerald+ mid-lane samples. They are statistical signals, not guarantees; player skill and jungle attention matter more than the number alone.

difficult.name: Vladimir
difficult.advice: Vladimir outsustains your early trades and can dodge your burst with Sanguine Pool. Punish him before he gets items, but do not chase him through his pool. Roam instead of forcing a lane kill.

difficult.name: Annie
difficult.advice: Annie's point-and-click stun is a direct answer to your E. Track her stun stacks, bait the stun with a short trade, and only all-in when it is down.

difficult.name: Vex
difficult.advice: Vex punishes dashes and long trades. Stay outside her fear range, farm with Q, and look for roams rather than dueling her in the wave.

difficult.name: Kassadin
difficult.advice: Kassadin scales and can escape your burst. Pressure him before level 6, then avoid wasting R on his Riftwalk. Ask for jungle help to close the game early.

favorable.name: Taliyah
favorable.advice: Taliyah is immobile once her worked ground is gone. Dodge her Q and E, then trade with Q-E-W when her knockup is down.

favorable.name: Syndra
favorable.advice: Syndra is vulnerable after she uses Scatter the Weak. Bait the stun, dodge the sphere, and all-in before her next rotation.

favorable.name: Zoe
favorable.advice: Zoe relies on hitting Sleepy Trouble Bubble. Keep minions between you and her, dodge the paddle star, and punish her when she steps forward.

mistakes: Entering before the enemy's crowd control is used.
Treating E as a free engage instead of keeping an exit.
Ignoring where daggers land.
Forcing R into a channel interrupt.
Chasing a second kill after the fight is already lost.
Copying an AD or on-hit build without practicing the auto-attack spacing.

practicePlan.title: Dagger landing drill
steps: In the practice tool, cast Q and W at different angles.
Walk to each dagger and call out whether picking it up is safe.
Repeat until you can predict the landing spot without watching the ground.

practicePlan.title: Reset chain drill
steps: Set up two target dummies and lower their health.
Kill one, pick up a dagger, then immediately decide whether to E to the second target or leave.
Do not chain blindly; say the exit route out loud.

practicePlan.title: Teamfight review
steps: Watch one replay per session.
Pause at every death and identify which enemy cooldown was available.
Write down one rule for the next game, such as 'wait for Annie stun'.

faq.q: Is Katarina hard to learn?
faq.a: Yes. Her difficulty is high because her damage depends on dagger placement, cooldown resets and fight timing. The mechanics are learnable, but the decision-making takes reps.

faq.q: What is Katarina's best build in patch 26.21?
faq.a: There is no single best build. AP burst with Lich Bane is the recommended default; the AD and on-hit core with Kraken Slayer, Gluttonous Greaves and Terminus is the most common Lolalytics path. Choose based on the game and your practice.

faq.q: What skill order should I use?
faq.a: Max Q, then E, then W, and take R at 6, 11 and 16. Start Q-E-W in most lanes.

faq.q: When should I use Death Lotus?
faq.a: After the enemy's reliable interrupts are used, or when you can hit multiple targets without being punished. Do not channel just because it is available.

faq.q: Is Katarina good for beginners?
faq.a: She is not the easiest first champion. If you are new, expect to lose fights while learning her entry timing; practice dagger pickups before taking her into ranked.

sett.h1: How to Play Sett in League of Legends
heroIntro: Sett is a top-lane juggernaut who wins short trades with his passive regeneration, Q auto-attack reset and E stun. His W, Haymaker, converts damage taken into a shield and a powerful true-damage punch.

This guide covers the patch 26.21 top-lane build, the exact skill path used by the highest-sample data, practical E-W-R combos, lane matchups and the mistakes that make Sett feel weak. It is based on Data Dragon 16.21.1 and current U.GG and Lolalytics samples.
sett.quickAnswer: Start W-E-Q, max Q first, then W, then E. Take Conqueror with Resolve secondaries, build Stridebreaker into Black Cleaver, and use E to stun before W so the true-damage center is unavoidable. Sett is strong in short trades and sidelane fights, but he is kited by ranged champions and should not waste Haymaker without grit.

quickStart.keyMechanic: Haymaker converts stored damage into a shield and true damage
quickStart.beginnerMistake: Casting W without grit or using E on only one side of the target
quickStart.winCondition: Win the side lane, force a flank with R, and use E-W to peel or delete a carry

abilities.name: Pit Grit
abilities.description: Sett's basic attacks alternate between a left punch and a stronger, faster right punch. He also regenerates health based on missing health.
tips: Use the right punch to last-hit and trade.
Your passive makes long, low-health fights more survivable.
Do not confuse regeneration with immunity; burst still kills you.
abilities.mistake: Trading at low health without tracking the enemy's burst.

abilities.name: Knuckle Down
abilities.description: Sett's next two attacks deal bonus damage based on the target's maximum health, and he gains movement speed toward enemy champions.
tips: Q is an auto-attack reset; use it immediately after an auto.
The speed helps you stay on a fleeing target.
Against high-health tanks, Q is a reliable damage source.
abilities.mistake: Using Q on minions and then having no reset for the champion trade.

abilities.name: Haymaker
abilities.description: Sett stores damage taken as grit. On cast, he consumes it for a shield and punches an area, dealing true damage in the center and physical damage at the sides.
tips: Let the enemy hit you first so the shield and punch are larger.
The center is the real threat; aim it at the target's current position.
You can Flash during the windup to reposition the punch.
abilities.mistake: Panic-casting W at full health with almost no grit.

abilities.name: Facebreaker
abilities.description: Sett pulls enemies from opposite sides together, damaging and stunning them. Enemies on only one side are slowed instead.
tips: Position so the enemy is between you and a minion or wall.
E stun sets up the W center.
Use E to interrupt dashes and channeled abilities.
abilities.mistake: Using E when all enemies are on one side and expecting a stun.

abilities.name: The Show Stopper
abilities.description: Sett carries an enemy champion through the air and slams them down, damaging and slowing nearby enemies.
tips: R can isolate a carry or peel a diver away from your team.
Use R to set up E on the landing zone.
Do not R a tank into your own backline.
abilities.mistake: Using R as a pure damage button and forgetting where the target will land.

explanation: Q is maxed first for reliable max-health damage and the movement speed to stay on targets.
W is maxed second because the shield and true-damage punch scale with ranks and decide extended fights.
E is maxed last; one point is enough for the stun and disruption early.
skillOrder.note: The W-E-Q start is the most common patch 26.21 path in the U.GG and Lolalytics samples. E start is a valid lane-specific choice when you need level 1 trading or a stun to secure a jungle gank.

combos.name: Standard E-W trade
combos.situation: A short trade when the enemy is between you and a minion or wall.
combos.execution: E pulls and stuns, Q resets your auto, auto twice, then W with the grit you stored. Aim the center at the target's landing position.
combos.mistake: Using W before the enemy has traded into you, so the shield and punch are small.
combos.warning: If E only hits one side, it slows instead of stunning; reposition before committing.

combos.name: R-E teamfight setup
combos.situation: A teamfight engage or sidelane pick when you can isolate a carry.
combos.execution: R the target into your team or away from theirs, E on landing to stun nearby enemies, Q for max-health damage, then W with the grit from the landing fight.
combos.mistake: R'ing a tank into your own backline and giving them a free engage.
combos.warning: Check where the target will land before using R; the slam can displace them away from your follow-up.

combos.name: Flash E pick
combos.situation: Punish a carry who is just outside E range.
combos.execution: Flash into E range, immediately E to stun, Q for the auto reset and W for the true-damage finish.
combos.mistake: Flashing without E ready, or using the combo without enough grit.
combos.warning: This spends your only reliable escape; do not use it without vision of the enemy jungler.

combos.name: Haymaker reposition
combos.situation: Reposition Haymaker's true-damage center onto a target who is walking out of range.
combos.execution: Start W, then Flash during the windup to place the center on the target.
combos.mistake: Flashing after the punch has already been released.
combos.warning: This is a high-commitment mechanic; practice it in the practice tool first.

sections.heading: Laning phase: short trades, then pressure
paragraphs: Sett's lane plan is built on short trades. Use E to stun, Q to reset your auto and W to absorb the response. Do not start with W; let the enemy commit damage first so the shield and punch are worth the cooldown.

Against ranged champions, give up early CS rather than walking into free poke. Doran's Shield, Second Wind and your passive regeneration let you survive until Stridebreaker. Against melee champions, contest the wave with E-Q trades and use the push to set up a cheater recall or a jungle dive.

At level 6, R gives you a dive and skirmish tool. Use it to isolate the enemy top laner under their tower only when you know where the enemy jungler is. Sett wins 1v2s when he has grit and a wall, not when he is caught in the open.
bullets: Do not E the wave if you need it to escape a gank.
Save W for the enemy's burst, not for a random poke trade.
A slow push is better than a fast push when you want to dive or roam.

sections.heading: Mid game: make the sidelane work
paragraphs: Sett's mid game is about sidelane pressure and forcing rotations. Push a side wave, threaten the tower, and make the enemy send someone to answer. When they do, your team can take an objective or you can flank with R.

In skirmishes, use E to peel for your carry or to stun multiple enemies. W is both defense and offense: the shield buys time, and the center punishes anyone who stands still. Do not chase ranged champions through open ground; let them come to you or force them into a wall.
bullets: Track your grit before you commit to W.
Use R to take the enemy carry out of the fight, not just for damage.
Hullbreaker is for games where you can actually pressure a sidelane.

sections.heading: Teamfights: frontline, then isolate
paragraphs: Sett is a frontline, but he is not unkillable. Start by peeling for your carry with E and R, then look for a Flash E on the enemy backline once their frontline is committed. If you are the primary engage, make sure your team can follow before you R in.

Haymaker is strongest after the enemy has spent damage on you. Do not waste it at the start of the fight just because it is off cooldown. A max-grit W can decide a teamfight; an empty W usually just delays your death.
bullets: E stun multiple targets if possible.
R the diver away from your carry.
Do not R a tank into your own team.

matchups.note: Win rates are from the U.GG patch 26.21 Emerald+ top-lane sample. Lolalytics lists Aatrox, Warwick and Ornn among Sett's hardest counters; U.GG highlights Tryndamere, Aatrox and Vayne. Treat these as signals, not fixed rules.

difficult.name: Tryndamere
difficult.advice: Tryndamere can match your sidelane and ignore your burst with Undying Rage. Take short trades, do not chase him through his ultimate, and buy armor or Thornmail if he is the win condition.

difficult.name: Aatrox
difficult.advice: Aatrox outranges you with his Q and sustains through your trades. Use E to interrupt his Q3 or dash, and avoid fighting in his sweet spots. Executioner's Calling or Thornmail can help.

difficult.name: Vayne
difficult.advice: Vayne kites you with Tumble and Silver Bolts. Do not chase through open ground; force her near a wall, use E to stun, and ask for jungle pressure.

favorable.name: Rumble
favorable.advice: Rumble wants to stand and burn you, which lets you store grit and land a big W. Use E to keep him in your range and avoid fighting inside his Equalizer.

favorable.name: Tahm Kench
favorable.advice: Tahm Kench is a long trade, and Sett likes long trades. Use Q max-health damage and save W for his devour or shield timing.

favorable.name: K'Sante
favorable.advice: K'Sante has to commit to melee range. E his dash, punish with Q-W, and do not let him R you through a wall without a follow-up plan.

mistakes: Casting W with no grit.
Using E on one side and expecting a stun.
Chasing ranged champions through open ground.
R'ing a tank into your own backline.
Building full damage when your team needs a frontline.
Ignoring the right-punch timing and losing early trades.

practicePlan.title: Grit drill
steps: In the practice tool, let a dummy hit you, then cast W at different grit amounts.
Compare the shield and center damage.
Practice holding W until the enemy commits, not until it is off cooldown.

practicePlan.title: E-W center drill
steps: Place two dummies on opposite sides.
E them together and immediately W the center.
Repeat until the stun-to-punch timing is automatic.

practicePlan.title: R-E setup
steps: R a dummy toward a wall or your team.
E on landing to stun the nearby target.
Practice choosing a landing zone that keeps the enemy in your team's range.

faq.q: Is Sett easy to play?
faq.a: Sett's entry barrier is low, but his ceiling is medium. The basic E-Q-W trade is simple; the hard part is managing grit, choosing R targets and not getting kited.

faq.q: What is Sett's best build in patch 26.21?
faq.a: Stridebreaker into Black Cleaver is the standard core. Sterak's Gage, Spear of Shojin and Warmog's are common follow-ups. Hullbreaker is for sidelane pressure, not every game.

faq.q: What skill order should I use?
faq.a: Start W-E-Q, max Q, then W, then E, and take R at 6, 11 and 16. That is the most common path in the patch 26.21 samples.

faq.q: How do I use Sett's W correctly?
faq.a: Store grit by taking damage, then use the shield to survive the enemy's burst and aim the center at their current position. Do not cast it at full health with no grit.

faq.q: Is Sett good in low elo?
faq.a: Yes. His straightforward trades and sidelane strength are effective in low elo, but he becomes harder to play as enemies learn to kite and dodge Haymaker.

ksante.name: K'Sante
ksante.title: the Pride of Nazumah
ksante.tagline: A high-skill tank who can peel, duel and kidnap a carry through a wall.
ksante.metaTitle: How to Play K'Sante in LoL: Runes, Build & Combos (Patch 26.21)
ksante.metaDescription: Learn how to play K'Sante top in League of Legends with patch 26.21 runes, Iceborn Gauntlet build, skill order, combos, matchups and tips.
ksante.h1: How to Play K'Sante in League of Legends
heroIntro: K'Sante is a top-lane tank with an unusually high skill ceiling. He can shield, dash, pull enemies with his Q, stun with W and use R to drag a target through a wall and transform into a damage-focused duelist.

This guide covers the patch 26.21 top-lane build, exact skill order, practical Q-W-R combos, lane and teamfight decisions, and the matchups that expose his weaknesses. It is based on Data Dragon 16.21.1 and current U.GG and Lolalytics samples.
ksante.quickAnswer: Start E-Q-W, max Q first, then E, then W. Take Grasp of the Undying with Precision secondaries, build Kaenic Rookern into Iceborn Gauntlet, and use Q2 to pull enemies into W or R. K'Sante is a low-win-rate, high-mastery champion on patch 26.21: he is strong when you land his crowd control and weak when you waste R or miss Q stacks.

quickStart.keyMechanic: Q2 shockwave pulls enemies into your W or R
quickStart.beginnerMistake: Using R without a wall or a follow-up plan
quickStart.winCondition: Survive the lane, control river fights with Q2-W, and use R to isolate the enemy carry

abilities.name: Dauntless Instinct
abilities.description: K'Sante's abilities mark targets to take more damage from his next attack. In All Out, he deals more damage with attacks and abilities.
tips: Auto-attack after each ability to consume the mark.
In All Out, your damage is higher but your defenses are lower.
Do not chase marks into the enemy backline without a plan.
abilities.mistake: Spamming abilities without weaving autos and losing the passive damage.

abilities.name: Ntofo Strikes
abilities.description: K'Sante strikes in a short line, slowing enemies. Hitting grants a stack; at two stacks, the next Q becomes a shockwave that pulls enemies in.
tips: Use Q to farm and to build stacks before a trade.
Q2 is your setup tool; pull enemies into W or R.
In All Out, Q has a lower cooldown.
abilities.mistake: Wasting Q2 on the wave when a fight is about to start.

abilities.name: Path Maker
abilities.description: K'Sante charges while taking reduced damage, then dashes, knocking back and stunning enemies. In All Out, it deals more damage but no longer knocks back or stuns.
tips: Hold W to block the enemy's burst, then release to stun.
Use W to interrupt dashes or channeled abilities.
In All Out, W is a damage tool, not crowd control.
abilities.mistake: Releasing W early and losing the damage reduction before the burst lands.

abilities.name: Footwork
abilities.description: K'Sante dashes and gains a shield. Targeting an ally increases range and shields both. In All Out, cooldown is reduced and speed is increased.
tips: Use E on an ally to escape or to shield both of you.
E is your main defensive dash; do not waste it for poke.
In All Out, E is your main chase and repositioning tool.
abilities.mistake: Using E aggressively with no shield value and no exit.

abilities.name: All Out
abilities.description: K'Sante knocks an enemy back through any wall in their path, then dashes after them and enters All Out, gaining damage and healing at the cost of defenses.
tips: Use R to isolate a carry or to escape a losing fight.
Check the wall angle before committing; the target must hit a wall to be displaced.
In All Out, play like a duelist, not a tank.
abilities.mistake: R'ing a target with no wall or follow-up and then dying in All Out.

explanation: Q is maxed first for wave control, poke and the Q2 pull.
E is maxed second for a stronger shield and lower cooldown, which is core to K'Sante's survivability.
W is maxed last because one point gives the stun and damage reduction; the later ranks are a bonus.
skillOrder.note: This is the most common patch 26.21 path in the U.GG and Lolalytics samples. Some lanes prefer Q at level 1 for poke; E start is the safer default.

runes.title: Grasp frontline
runes.summary: Grasp of the Undying is the default keystone on patch 26.21. It rewards short trades, improves lane sustain and scales with K'Sante's health. Precision secondary adds tenacity, ability haste and last-stand damage.

keystone.name: Grasp of the Undying
keystone.why: Best default for short trades and health scaling.

primaryRunes.name: Demolish
primaryRunes.why: Tower pressure after a lane win.

primaryRunes.name: Second Wind
primaryRunes.why: Sustain against poke and short trades.

primaryRunes.name: Overgrowth
primaryRunes.why: Bonus health improves your shield, damage and frontline durability.

secondaryRunes.name: Legend: Haste
secondaryRunes.why: More Q and E casts in fights.

secondaryRunes.name: Last Stand
secondaryRunes.why: K'Sante often fights at low health in All Out.

notes: This is a common patch 26.21 setup, not the only correct page.
Grasp is weaker in lanes where you cannot safely auto-attack the enemy; in those games, Aftershock can be more reliable.
Do not take Demolish if you expect to be camped and cannot push.

summonerSpells.name: Flash
summonerSpells.why: Core for R angles, E escapes and W stuns.

summonerSpells.name: Ignite
summonerSpells.why: Adds kill pressure and helps win the level 6 all-in.
summonerSpells.alternative: Teleport is the safer choice in lanes where you expect to be poked out or need to match a sidelane.

builds.label: Tank core
builds.summary: K'Sante's default build prioritizes durability and ability haste. Kaenic Rookern covers magic damage, Mercury's Treads reduces crowd control, and Iceborn Gauntlet gives armor, spellblade damage and a slow.

items.why: Health, armor and magic resist make it the most common start in the Lolalytics sample.

items.name: Health Potion

items.name: Iceborn Gauntlet

Mercury's Treads is the default, but Plated Steelcaps is better against auto-attack-heavy teams.
Do not buy pure damage items on K'Sante unless you are already far ahead and can end the game.

builds.label: All Out duelist
builds.summary: When you are ahead and need to threaten the backline yourself, lean into ability haste and healing. This build is less forgiving and should not replace the tank core in even games.

Only consider this path when your team already has a reliable frontline.
If you are behind, build the tank core and play for picks, not duels.

combos.name: Q2 pull all-in
combos.situation: A standard all-in when you have two Q stacks and the enemy is in range.
combos.execution: Land the first Q, use the second Q shockwave to pull the target, E in for the shield, auto to consume the passive mark, W to stun, then R through a wall if the angle is available.
combos.mistake: Using Q2 too early and having no pull for the all-in.
combos.warning: Do not R unless the target will hit a wall or your team can follow.

combos.name: Ally E engage
combos.situation: Engage or disengage with an ally as the anchor.
combos.execution: E to an ally for the longer dash and shared shield, Q to stack and slow, W to block damage and stun, then R the priority target.
combos.mistake: Using E on an ally when you need it to escape.
combos.warning: E on an ally puts you next to them; make sure that is where you want to fight.

combos.name: Wall kidnap
combos.situation: Isolating a carry in a sidelane or river fight.
combos.execution: R the target through a wall, follow with E, use Q for damage and stacks, and W as a damage tool in All Out. Auto between abilities to consume passive marks.
combos.mistake: R'ing without a wall and then fighting in All Out with reduced defenses.
combos.warning: All Out is a commitment; check your exit before you use it.

combos.name: W into pull
combos.situation: Setting up a pick when the enemy is grouped.
combos.execution: Charge W to reduce incoming damage, release to stun, hit Q2 to pull them back into your team, then R the isolated target through a wall.
combos.mistake: Releasing W before the enemy commits their damage.
combos.warning: This combo requires your team to follow; do not start it alone.

sections.heading: Laning phase: controlled trades
paragraphs: K'Sante's lane is about controlled trades, not constant aggression. Use Q to farm and build stacks, E to shield the enemy's response, and W to block their key damage. Grasp auto-attacks are valuable, but do not walk into a losing trade just to proc it.

Against ranged tops, give up CS and preserve health. Doran's Helm, Second Wind and your shield let you survive; once you have Kaenic Rookern and Mercury's Treads, you can contest waves more confidently. Against melee tops, use Q2 to set up short E-Q-W trades and save R for a guaranteed wall angle.

At level 6, K'Sante becomes a pick threat. R can drag an overextended laner through a wall and into your jungler, but it also removes your tank stats. Only commit when you know where the enemy jungler is or when your lane opponent is already low.
bullets: Do not waste Q2 on the wave before a fight.
Use W to block the enemy's burst, not to poke.
Keep E for the enemy's engage or for an ally shield.

sections.heading: Mid game: control the river
paragraphs: K'Sante's mid game is about frontline presence and picks. Push a side wave, then group with your team around vision. Your Q2 pull and W stun can start a fight, but you should usually be the second or third champion in, not the first.
Use R to isolate a carry who steps too far forward or to peel a diver away from your own carry. In All Out, you are a duelist: chase only if the target is isolated and your team can cover the exit.
bullets: Play around walls; they are part of your R range.
E to an ally when you need a safe retreat.
Do not chase kills in All Out if your team is losing the fight.

sections.heading: Teamfights: peel first, then isolate
paragraphs: In teamfights, K'Sante is a peel-first frontline. Stand between the enemy engage and your carry, use Q2 to pull divers off, and W to stun the first threat. R is best used to remove a carry from the fight or to peel a diver away, not as a random damage button.
When you go All Out, your defenses drop. Commit only when the enemy's crowd control is used or when you can finish the target quickly. If the fight turns, E back to an ally and reset the frontline.
bullets: Q2 pull is your best setup.
W charge blocks burst; do not release early.
All Out is a commitment, not a free stat boost.

matchups.note: Win rates are from the U.GG patch 26.21 Emerald+ top-lane sample. Lolalytics lists Poppy, Kayle and Garen as K'Sante's hardest counters. K'Sante's overall win rate is low, so treat matchup numbers as context and focus on the mechanical interaction.

difficult.name: Poppy
difficult.advice: Poppy's Steadfast Presence stops your dashes and makes E and R unreliable. Play for short Q trades, bait her W, and do not commit to All Out while it is up.

difficult.name: Kayle
difficult.advice: Kayle outscales you and can kite your All Out. Pressure her before level 6, ask for jungle help, and avoid long lanes where she can free-hit.

difficult.name: Garen
difficult.advice: Garen's silence stops your W and E, and his execute punishes low-health All Out fights. Use Q2 to keep distance, and do not R him while his spin is active.

difficult.name: Fiora
difficult.advice: Fiora can parry your W and punish your vitals. Do not R into her Riposte; bait it with a short trade, then commit.

favorable.name: Warwick
favorable.advice: Warwick wants to drain-tank through extended fights. Your Q2 pull and W stun can interrupt his sustain, and your shield helps survive his burst.

favorable.name: Cho'Gath
favorable.advice: Cho'Gath is a large, immobile target. Land Q2, use W to block his engage, and punish him with Grasp trades.

favorable.name: Kennen
favorable.advice: Kennen wants to kite and flank. Keep Q2 available to pull him out of Lightning Rush, and use W to block his burst when he commits.

mistakes: Wasting Q2 on the wave.
Using R without a wall or follow-up.
Releasing W before the enemy's burst.
Forgetting to auto-attack after abilities for the passive mark.
Fighting in All Out with no exit.
Building damage when the team needs a frontline.

practicePlan.title: Q2 pull drill
steps: Stack Q on a dummy, then use Q2 to pull a second dummy.
Immediately W to stun both.
Repeat until the pull-to-stun timing is consistent.

practicePlan.title: Wall R angles
steps: Open the practice tool near different walls.
Practice R'ing a dummy through each wall.
Identify which angles put the target in your team's range.

practicePlan.title: All Out limit test
steps: Enter All Out against a durable dummy.
Practice auto-weaving and E repositioning.
Leave All Out before you would die in a real fight.

faq.q: Is K'Sante hard to play?
faq.a: Yes. He is one of the highest-skill tanks in the game because his Q stacks, W charge, R walls and All Out form change his role in a fight.

faq.q: What is K'Sante's best build in patch 26.21?
faq.a: Kaenic Rookern, Mercury's Treads and Iceborn Gauntlet is the standard core. Spirit Visage and Unending Despair are common follow-ups. Pure damage builds are situational.

faq.q: What skill order should I use?
faq.a: Start E-Q-W, max Q, then E, then W, and take R at 6, 11 and 16. That is the most common patch 26.21 path.

faq.q: Why is K'Sante's win rate low?
faq.a: His kit is complex and his All Out form trades defense for damage, which makes him easy to punish if you misjudge the fight. The best K'Sante players perform much better than the overall average.

faq.q: When should I use All Out?
faq.a: When you can isolate a carry, finish a low-health target, or escape a losing fight through a wall. Do not use it just because it is available.

ksante.statsNote: U.GG and Lolalytics use different samples and ranking methods. Both snapshots are from patch 26.21, Emerald+ and global ranked Solo/Duo. K'Sante's overall win rate is below 50%, but Lolalytics reports a much higher win rate for the best K'Sante players, which reflects his high mastery curve.

heroIntro: Azir is a high-skill mid-lane champion who controls the battlefield through his Sand Soldiers. Unlike most mages, Azir relies on positioning, soldier placement and extended damage windows rather than simply casting spells at enemies.
To master Azir, you need to understand how to manage your soldiers, trade safely in lane, position during teamfights and recognize when an aggressive play is worth the risk.
azir.quickAnswer: Azir: max W > Q > E, use Lethal Tempo, and follow the Azir sustained AP core as a patch 26.21 baseline. Read the matchup notes below and adapt your items to the enemy composition.

quickStart.keyMechanic: Positioning and commanding Sand Soldiers to control space
quickStart.beginnerMistake: Using E aggressively without an exit plan. A dash into the enemy team can leave you exposed.
quickStart.winCondition: Deal sustained damage from a safe position and control space around objectives

abilities.name: Shurima's Legacy
abilities.description: Azir can summon the Sun Disc on eligible destroyed turret ruins. This temporary structure can help defend or pressure an area when used at the right time.
tips: Treat the Sun Disc as a situational objective tool rather than a reason to take unnecessary risks around a turret ruin.

abilities.name: Conquering Sands
abilities.description: Azir commands his active Sand Soldiers to dash toward a target location, damaging and slowing enemies along their path.
tips: Reposition soldiers to reach enemies who are outside their current attack range.
Use the slow to make subsequent soldier attacks easier to land.
Avoid spending Q carelessly if you need to preserve your repositioning options.

abilities.name: Arise!
abilities.description: Azir summons a Sand Soldier. His soldiers attack enemies in a line when he commands attacks against targets within their range.
tips: Place soldiers where you can farm while maintaining a safe distance.
Position them to threaten the enemy's approach to the minion wave.
Track your available soldiers and their remaining duration.
Avoid placing every soldier where it can be ignored or where you cannot safely use it.

abilities.name: Shifting Sands
abilities.description: Azir dashes toward one of his Sand Soldiers and gains a shield. If he collides with an enemy champion, he stops and gains a charge of W.
tips: Keep a soldier in a position that gives you a possible escape route.
Use E defensively when an enemy jungler or laner threatens you.
Use it offensively only when you understand where you will land and how you will get out.

abilities.name: Emperor's Divide
abilities.description: Azir summons a line of soldiers that surges forward, damaging and knocking back enemies. The soldiers then form a temporary wall that enemies cannot pass through normally, while allies can cross it.
tips: Disrupt enemies diving onto your carries.
Separate frontline champions from their backline.
Punish enemies who move through narrow spaces.
Use the knockback to peel for yourself when an assassin reaches you.

combos.name: Basic poke
combos.execution: Place a Sand Soldier and attack an enemy within its range. Use this to pressure opponents while keeping your own champion at a safe distance.
combos.mistake: Adapt the sequence to the situation; do not execute it automatically.

combos.name: Extended trade
combos.execution: Place a soldier, attack through it, reposition it with Q and continue attacking if the situation is safe. Do not automatically extend every trade. Enemy cooldowns, minion damage and jungle pressure matter.
combos.mistake: Adapt the sequence to the situation; do not execute it automatically.

combos.name: Defensive escape
combos.execution: Place a soldier toward a safe direction and dash to it with E when you need to disengage. This requires enough distance and a valid soldier target. Plan the route before you are forced to use it.
combos.mistake: Adapt the sequence to the situation; do not execute it automatically.

combos.name: Engage or displacement
combos.execution: Azir can dash toward a soldier and cast his ultimate to displace enemies. This can create a powerful teamfight opportunity, but it also places him close to danger. Use it when your team can follow up and the enemy's defensive abilities are accounted for. Important: The famous Azir shuffle is a situational advanced technique, not the default way to use your ultimate. Learn the underlying E and R interactions in Practice Tool before attempting it in ranked games.

sections.heading: Laning Phase
paragraphs: Your first objective is to farm consistently while learning how far you can safely threaten the opponent with your soldiers.
Azir can become vulnerable when his mobility tool is unavailable. Before pushing the wave, consider where the enemy jungler could approach from.
bullets: Use soldier range to trade without walking directly into the enemy's threat range.
Watch the enemy jungler before using E aggressively.
Avoid using Q solely for small amounts of damage if it leaves you without a useful repositioning option.
Learn how much damage your soldiers deal to minions so you do not accidentally disrupt your farming.
Respect champions who can reach you quickly or interrupt your positioning.

sections.heading: Mid and Late Game
paragraphs: Azir's value comes from sustained damage and controlling space around objectives.
You do not always need a spectacular shuffle to win a fight. Consistent damage, safe positioning and a well-timed defensive ultimate can be more valuable.
bullets: Position behind your frontline when possible.
Place soldiers where enemies must walk through or around them.
Avoid chasing a low-health enemy so far that you lose your safe position.
Save your ultimate when enemy divers are a serious threat to your backline.
Use narrow terrain to make your soldier attacks and ultimate more difficult to avoid.

sections.heading: Final Advice
paragraphs: Mastering Azir is about controlling space, not simply landing flashy combos. Learn to position soldiers efficiently, maintain safe damage windows and use Emperor's Divide according to what your team needs in each fight.

mistakes: Using E aggressively without an exit plan. A dash into the enemy team can leave you exposed.
Wasting Q. Repositioning soldiers is central to your damage and control.
Standing too close to the frontline. Your range is useful only if you preserve it.
Overusing the shuffle. An unreliable engage can cost a teamfight.
Ignoring soldier placement. Poor positioning reduces your damage and makes it easier for enemies to engage on you.

practicePlan.title: Practice 1
steps: In Practice Tool, focus on one skill at a time:
The goal is not to execute the fastest combo immediately. It is to make the correct decision and execute it consistently.
Keep moving while maintaining soldier attack range.

practicePlan.title: Practice 2
steps: Practise W–AA–Q–AA without losing track of your champion's position.
Rehearse E escape routes from common gank angles.

faq.q: Is Azir difficult to learn?
faq.a: Yes. Azir requires strong positioning, soldier management and an understanding of when to use his mobility defensively or offensively.

faq.q: What is Azir's most important ability?
faq.a: W is central to his identity because his Sand Soldiers enable his primary damage pattern. However, Q, E and R are all essential to controlling space and surviving fights.

faq.q: Should you always use Azir's ultimate to engage?

Aim Wind Slash at weakened targets rather than firing it without considering their remaining health.
Remember that the ultimate can be valuable even before you commit to a kill, because it strengthens your threat during the window.

sections.heading: Laning Phase
paragraphs: Riven is strongest when she can control the timing of trades and use her mobility efficiently.
Wave management is important because Riven is melee and must often approach the minion wave to farm. Consider whether you can safely walk up before committing your cooldowns.
bullets: Track enemy cooldowns before committing to a longer trade.
Use short trades when the opponent has a stronger extended fight.
Preserve enough mobility to disengage if the enemy jungler may be nearby.
Learn when to use the third Q cast for damage, crowd control or movement.
Avoid spending every ability on the wave if the opponent can punish your cooldowns.

sections.heading: Mid and Late Game
paragraphs: Riven can threaten isolated targets and dive onto vulnerable backline champions, but her success depends on timing.
Your goal is to create a favourable damage window, not simply to use every ability as quickly as possible.
bullets: Look for flanks instead of always approaching through the enemy frontline.
Wait for key enemy crowd-control abilities before committing when possible.
Use E to absorb damage and reposition rather than treating it as a free engage.
Do not confuse mobility with invulnerability.
If a direct dive is too risky, protect your carries or focus on a nearby target you can reach safely.

sections.heading: Final Advice
paragraphs: Riven rewards deliberate execution. Learn to combine movement, basic attacks and ability timing before chasing advanced combos. Consistent trades and good decisions will matter more than memorizing a long sequence of buttons.

mistakes: Ignoring Runic Blade. Failing to weave basic attacks wastes part of her damage pattern.
Using every Q cast immediately. You may lose flexibility in spacing and timing.
Spending E to engage without a plan. You may have no shielded escape when the enemy responds.
Starting fights before checking enemy cooldowns. Crowd control can stop your damage sequence.
Treating every combo as a fixed script. Riven must adapt to range, target movement and the state of the fight.

Learn the barrel's health countdown and attack timing.

Use the slow to make follow-up attacks easier.
Powder Keg is the core of Gangplank's most distinctive damage patterns.

matchups.note: Counter trends are from Lolalytics patch 16.21 Emerald+ for this role. They are statistical signals, not hard counters in every game; lane skill, team composition and jungle pressure still matter.

difficult.name: Kayle
difficult.advice: Use barrels to control the wave and deny free scaling. Coordinate pressure before she reaches her strongest levels.

difficult.name: Sion
difficult.advice: Use barrels to contest the wave and punish his Q charge. Prioritize scaling and objective value over repeated all-ins.

difficult.name: Gwen
difficult.advice: Keep barrels between you, save W for key control, and avoid extended fights inside her mist.

favorable.name: Illaoi
favorable.advice: Farm outside her threat with Q and barrels, sidestep E, and avoid standing near multiple tentacles. W can cleanse her slow, not undo damage.

favorable.name: Renekton
favorable.advice: Maintain distance and punish his approach with barrels. Track his fury and avoid close trades when it is high.

favorable.name: Yasuo
favorable.advice: Space barrels so he cannot dash through the wave to reach you. Avoid placing a key barrel where Wind Wall blocks your setup.
